entities.summary: Jean-François Leriget de La Faye was a French diplomat and art collector who played a significant role in the diplomatic efforts of the French monarchy during the early 18th century. As a member of the Académie française, he contributed to the development of French literature and culture. De La Faye's legacy is marked by his efforts to promote French interests abroad and his role in shaping the cultural and artistic landscape of 18th-century Europe. The French diplomat's diplomatic career was marked by his service as a French ambassador to several European courts, including the courts of Austria and England. His diplomatic efforts were instrumental in securing trade agreements and cultural exchanges between France and its European neighbors. De La Faye's artistic collection, which included works by artists such as Nicolas Poussin and Jean-Honore Fragonard, helped to establish France as a major center for artistic innovation during the 18th century. De La Faye's diplomatic career was also marked by his involvement in several high-profile diplomatic incidents, including the Affair of the Diamond Necklace, which highlighted the tensions between France and its European rivals. The French diplomat's legacy is still felt today, as his diplomatic efforts and artistic collection continue to inspire scholars and art lovers alike.
